Case :- Writ - C No. - 9074 of 2023
Petitioner :- Smt. Sheela

Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Sudeep Harkauli

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Pritinker Diwaker,Chief Justice Hon'ble Ashutosh Srivastava,J.
1.
Heard Shri Sudeep Harkauli, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. Meenakshi Singh, learned Addl.
Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondent.

2. The challenge in this writ petition is to the award dated 15.2.2023 passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Moradabad under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 in respect of land acquired for the purpose of construction scheme Ganga Expressway by Uttar Pradesh Industrial Development Authority in District Sambhal.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. The challenge to the award aforesaid is being laid on the ground that the land of the petitioner acquired was commercial in nature and yet compensation towards the same has been determined Smt. Sheela vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 7 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69442947/
1 treating the same to be agricultural.

entities.text: Sheela vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. At the very out set, learned counsel for the petitioner fairly submits that petitioner has an alternative remedy to file reference under Section 64 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He further submits that as the order impugned is patently illegally, writ petition can also be entertained.

5. On the other hand, learned Addl. Chief Standing Counsel submits that as the petitioner has an alternative remedy of filing the reference under Section 64 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, this Court may not interfere with the impugned order.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. Without entering into the merits of the case, petition is disposed of permitting the petitioner to withdraw this writ petition with liberty to file reference under Section 64 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
7. Needless to state, in the eventuality of filing any such reference within three weeks' from today,
the authority concerned shall decide the same on merits ignoring the point of limitation.
